answer: An agent economy can require each participant to post a refundable bond before it can submit jobs, and slash that bond when a dispute proves fraud. A reputation-weighted task market then limits each new identity to low-value work until it completes verified jobs; making one identity into a falcon, violet, or cipher does not bypass that history. A sybil attacker must lock capital in every account and risk losing it, so identities are costly rather than free.
